title: Big Deal
content: Meaning/Usage: Something really important. Often times used with "no" to express that the event is not as important as they think. Explanation: This phrase is also used sarcastically. For example, if someone says "I did 30 push-ups this morning." Someone else can respond, "Big deal. I did 50 push-ups!" "Passing my driver's test was no big deal." "He thinks he is such a big deal." "It's no big deal if we don't go tonight." A. "I think I might have lost that screwdriver you let me borrow last week." B. "It's no big deal, I have another one." Other Common Sentences "He thinks he is all that matters." "It's not that important."

examples.sentence: Passing my driver's test was no big deal.
He thinks he is such a big deal.
It's no big deal if we don't go tonight.
I think I might have lost that screwdriver you let me borrow last week.
It's no big deal, I have another one.
He thinks he is all that matters.
